newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin says no plan to seek foreign help on wages.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin says no plan to seek foreign help on wages.

text.p: The Kremlin denied a report by Itar-Tass news agency on Friday which quoted President Boris Yeltsin as saying Russia may seek foreign assistance to pay wage arrears to public sector workers.
Tass reported Yeltsin as saying Russia might turn to foreign leaders for help in paying the arrears. But a Kremlin press service statement said: "This information does not correspond to reality."

Tass quoted Yeltsin as saying at a meeting with Russian regional leaders that external, as well as domestic sources, would be needed to pay the huge arrears to public sector workers, such as teachers and doctors, within three months.
"Let's turn to leaders of foreign countries," Tass quoted him as saying.
There was no immediate explanation from Tass. Brief television footage of the meeting did not include the remark.

Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais, sitting beside Yeltsin, told him it was impossible to pay all backlogged wages in three months. But Yeltsin, in televised remarks and looking flustered, said: "It is possible if we all pull together."
